speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned difficulty conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity; to better understand your condition, how long have you been trying to conceive, and can you describe the specific type of pain you feel?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vaginismus (likely secondary to body dysmorphic disorder). Given the 15 months of unsuccessful conception, the husband's occasional erectile difficulties, and the patient's reported pelvic floor muscle tension during penetration, the clinical picture strongly supports a diagnosis of vaginismus. No further diagnostic tests are required at this time; management will focus on psychotherapy and pelvic floor physical therapy.
